title: NASA completes testing on dual-mode propulsion CubeSat ahead of launch
excerpt: The ASCENT Propulsion Dual Mode mission is manifested to launch no earlier than October 1 on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.
bodyHtml:
Engineers at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, completed a series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite, according to NASA. The ASCENT Propulsion Dual Mode mission is manifested to launch no earlier than October 1 as a payload aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

The ASCENT Propulsion Dual Mode mission is a flight demonstration of a spacecraft about the size of a large shoebox. The spacecraft uses a single non-toxic propellant called ASCENT to feed both a high-thrust combustion engine and low-thrust electrospray thrusters from one central tank, saving critical mass and volume.

Testing inside Marshall's Small Spacecraft Servicing and Integration Lab included a pressurized helium leak test of the spacecraft inside a vacuum chamber. The team also subjected the spacecraft to thermal vacuum testing and a spin test to measure the spacecraft's mass properties and center of gravity.

Once deployed into an orbit about 325 miles above Earth, the spacecraft will begin a nine-month mission. The operations team will execute short chemical and electric maneuvers, followed by orbit-raising and lowering maneuvers to prove the dual-mode concept works in space.
